segments.caption: Day 3 of 100 Days of Machine Learning: your first ML project, step by step.
Problem definition, data collection, data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, the train-test split, model training and evaluation, with the actual code. Save this one!
Most beginners watch hours of theory and never build anything.
Today we build one real project together: predicting flat prices in Bangalore. Follow along.
Step 1, problem definition: write one sentence.
Predict the flat price in lakhs, using area, bedrooms, location and age. Success means being off by less than 8 lakh on average.
If you can't write this sentence, don't start coding.
Step 2, data collection: get the data.
Free sources: Kaggle, data.gov.in, or your own spreadsheet.
For a first project, a few thousand rows is plenty.
Load it with pandas, using read_csv. We have 10,000 flats.
Step 3, data cleaning: run these 4 checks, every single time.
1, missing values: isnull().sum().
2, duplicates: drop_duplicates().
3, impossible values: describe(). 12,000 sq ft with 1 bedroom? Probably a typo.
4, outliers. One 50 crore villa will confuse a flat price model.
Then fix them: fill missing values with the median, delete the duplicates, and correct or remove the typos.
Step 4, exploratory data analysis, or EDA: make 3 plots before any model.
Price versus area. Average price by area of the city. And a histogram of prices.
Here, price climbs steadily with size, and Koramangala costs the most.
Step 5, the train-test split: split before you train.
train_test_split, with test_size = 0.2. Then lock the test set away until the very end.
Step 6, model training: start simple.
Linear regression, in 3 lines: create the model, fit it on the training data, and predict. Fancy models can wait.
Step 7, model evaluation: compare with a dumb baseline.
Just guessing the average price is off by 22 lakh. Our model is off by 7. That's under our target of 8. It works!
That number is the mean absolute error: on average, how far each prediction is from the real price.
Want others to use it? That's deployment: wrap it in a free Streamlit app, and retrain when new sales come in.
Here's the whole checklist. Screenshot it.
One sentence goal. Load the data. 4 cleaning checks. 3 plots. Split. Simple model. Beat the baseline.
Save this, and send it to the friend who keeps saying they'll start ML someday.
Your turn: you've just loaded a new dataset. What's the first thing you run? Vote in the caption poll!
Tomorrow, Day 4: cleaning messy data, hands-on.
Follow for data science made simple!
